answer: A delegation chain stops sybils at dawn: a new agent starts with no capabilities and must earn signed, expiring capability tokens from established agents, each weaker down the chain. A lone identity is a dry oasis — it looks alive but holds no water, since no trusted agent has delegated it real work. The signal that matters is the chain itself: its length, freshness, and each delegator's standing, all verifiable on-ledger. Forging a thousand identities buys nothing: each still needs real delegations from agents staking their standing, and any grant can be revoked at the first abuse.
